question: Should ClawHub reject case-colliding package paths at every publish and import boundary, including legacy lowercase aliases and directory-case collisions, even though existing packages that were accepted can no longer be published or imported unchanged?
rationale: The branch is coherent and well-proven, but it changes the registry’s acceptance contract rather than repairing behavior already guaranteed by current code or docs.

options.title: Adopt portable package validation
options.body: Accept the compatibility break to prevent packages that cannot round-trip safely on case-insensitive filesystems, then merge this centralized enforcement.

options.title: Narrow the rejected set
options.body: Limit enforcement to a smaller maintainer-defined set of manifest paths or collision cases and update the shared helper plus focused tests before merge.

options.title: Retain permissive ingestion
options.body: Keep accepting existing case-colliding packages and close or redesign this PR if cross-platform portability is not a registry requirement.

recommendation.title: Adopt portable package validation
recommendation.body: Accept the compatibility break to prevent packages that cannot round-trip safely on case-insensitive filesystems, then merge this centralized enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter supplied the concrete cross-platform failure motivating the policy, though repository ownership evidence is weak.
